description: Reproduced from user zip (bw-repro). go-git v5.17.0 (and upstream main) storage/filesystem/dotgit/dotgit.go objectPacks() only discovers packs named pack-<hash>.pack. C git reads any *.idx in objects/pack. git's 'loose-objects' maintenance task (daily under maintenance.strategy=incremental, enabled by 'git maintenance start'/'register' and Scalar) writes loose-<hash>.pack. Run 1 packs loose objects but leaves them on disk (bw still works); run 2 prune-packed deletes the loose copies -> objects exist only in loose-*.pack -> bw sees 'object not found' (sync: 'walk remote commits: object not found'; list: 'open treefs: read commit: object not found'). NOT caused by geometric repack or gc --auto (verified: those only write pack-*). Workaround: git repack -a -d (verified on both repos); prevent recurrence with git config maintenance.loose-objects.enabled false. Fix options: (a) detect non-pack- packs on open and error with actionable message / auto-repack via execGit; (b) patch go-git pack discovery (needs path-based API, objectPackPath builds pack-<hash>). Related: bw-gh-138 (stale handle after fetch, different).

comments.text: Upstream: go-git issue #2345 (2026-08-26) is this exact bug. PR #2346 (2026-08-27) fixes it but targets main/v6, is 47 files +2811/-1895 tangled with a packhandle refactor, CONFLICTING, no reviews, no v5 backport. bw is on v5.17.0; latest v5.19.2 and v6.0.0-alpha.5 still filter on pack- prefix. Waiting on upstream is not viable. Plan: billy fs shim in bw that aliases loose-<hash>.{pack,idx} as pack-<hash>.* for go-git's dotgit discovery; delete when an adoptable go-git release fixes discovery.

title: [BUG] go-git ignores loose-*.pack written by git maintenance loose-objects task; bw fails with object not found
